final_outcome: Development split materialization and readback accept verified reference-backed (v2) releases with v1 parity, distinct input and output limits and safe failures. The working tree is uncommitted, increment 6 is still unreviewed and M2's exit gate remains open.
important_decisions: Dispatch the existing split entry points on the validated release version. The split document, rules and ordering stay v1. Only release lineage differs by version.
Reuse one rule implementation. An opt-in max_inventory_records keyword streams the identical canonical-array digest and defaults to the legacy single-document bound.
Take the population from the same all-or-nothing restore verification, not a second reader.
Bound the split output, not the inventory: reject above 7,133 rows before derivation and fail an exact 1 MiB size check before the output directory exists. No truncation or schema change.
DocumentSizeError subclasses ContractError with an unchanged message so size limits are distinguishable without changing any handler.
Classify L1 because no rule, schema or wire contract changes. Any such change is L2.
No conflict with the frozen architecture. The 1 MiB JSON split is a capacity constraint, since specification 12.2 treats JSON and Parquet as selected defaults.
known_blockers: M2 exit gate remains open pending authorized real data, defensible chronology, property evidence, reviewed policies and isolated reproducible evaluation.
A complete JSON split never holds more than 7,128 observations, and 2,673 always fit. A larger or longer-identifier real release needs a reviewed versioned split transport, an L2 wire change.
V2 candidates keep the 4 MiB source and 1 MiB lineage caps, so a release near the M0-documented 4,528 rows also needs bounded source and lineage transport.
Exact-tree Linux CI awaits separately authorized source publication.
